# Instruction: The State of Global Education — Progress, Gaps, and Inequality

## Overview

Create an A1 portrait poster for public exhibition that tells a compelling data story about global education. The narrative arc is one of **dramatic progress followed by a sobering reality check**: humanity has gone from fewer than 1-in-5 adults being educated to more than 4-in-5 — yet 244 million children remain out of school, and in the poorest countries, children receive fewer than 3 years of quality schooling compared to 10+ in wealthy nations. The audience is the general public, so clarity and visual impact matter more than academic detail.

## Key Priorities

- **The "progress vs. gaps" contrast is the heart of the poster.** The historical transformation (1800 → today) should feel triumphant, but the learning crisis and out-of-school figures must land with equal weight — don't let one overshadow the other.
- **Make the 244 million children stat visually dominant.** This is the number viewers should remember after walking away.
- **The comparison between quality schooling in the poorest vs. richest countries (< 3 years vs. 10+ years)** should be immediately graspable — consider a bold side-by-side or bar contrast.

## Visual & Style Guidance

Adopt a **data-forward yet engaging** tone. Use a clean, modern layout with generous whitespace. Think deep navy or charcoal backgrounds with warm accent colors (amber, coral) to highlight key figures. Typography should be bold and hierarchical — large numerals for headline stats, concise labels beneath. Infographic elements (icon arrays, simple bar comparisons) are welcome; avoid clutter. The overall mood should feel serious and authoritative but accessible — not academic, not flashy.

2. Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json` for poster requirements, sections, metrics, and style definitions.

2. The poster must be a single self-contained image file.

# The State of Global Education: Progress, Gaps, and Inequality

A data-driven comparison of how education access, quality, and equity have evolved worldwide — and where critical challenges remain.

## Two Centuries of Educational Expansion

In the early 1800s, fewer than 1 in 5 adults worldwide had received any formal education. Education was a luxury reserved for a small elite. Over the past two centuries, this ratio has reversed dramatically. Today, more than 4 in 5 adults (aged 15+) have received some formal primary, secondary, or tertiary education. Literacy rates have followed a similar trajectory: two centuries ago, very few could read and write; now, the vast majority of adults possess basic literacy skills.

## The Learning Crisis: Being in School ≠ Learning

International statistics often track enrollment and attendance as markers of progress. However, being enrolled does not guarantee quality learning. In many lower-income countries, fewer than 20% of children achieve minimum reading proficiency by the end of primary school — meaning they cannot identify key ideas in a text or connect them to their own experiences. The data reveals a stark learning crisis hidden behind enrollment numbers.

## 244 Million Children Still Out of School

Despite enormous progress, approximately 244 million children of official school age were not enrolled in primary or secondary education in 2023. A major driver is secondary-level dropout: many children who complete primary school do not continue. The following table summarizes the scale of the challenge:

| Indicator | Value (2023) |
|---|---|
| Children out of school (all levels) | ~244 million |
| Primary-age children out of school | ~60 million |
| Secondary-age adolescents out of school | ~184 million |

## Learning-Adjusted Years of Schooling: A World Divided

Researchers combine the quantity and quality of education into a single metric called "learning-adjusted years of schooling." The disparities are enormous:

| Country Group | Learning-Adjusted Years of Schooling (2020) |
|---|---|
| Poorest countries (parts of Sub-Saharan Africa) | < 3 years |
| South Asia & Sub-Saharan Africa average | < 7 years |
| High-income countries | 10+ years |

Children in the world's poorest nations receive less than a third of the quality schooling available to their peers in wealthy countries. Most of the world's children live in South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa, where the average remains below 7 years.

## Closing the Gender Gap

Historically, boys were far more likely to attend school than girls. Today, the global gender gap in enrollment has largely closed across primary and secondary education. At the tertiary level, young women are now more likely to be enrolled than young men.

| Education Level | Gender Gap Status (2023) |
|---|---|
| Primary | Nearly closed globally |
| Secondary | Nearly closed globally |
| Tertiary | Women now exceed men in enrollment |

However, significant exceptions persist. In countries like Afghanistan, girls remain far less likely to attend school at any level.

## Key Takeaway

The world has achieved remarkable progress — but the job is far from done. Hundreds of millions of children are either out of school or learning very little while in it. Closing the gap between enrollment and actual learning, and between rich and poor nations, is one of the most pressing challenges of our time.

# The State of Global Education: Progress, Gaps, and Inequality

A data-driven comparison of how education access, quality, and equity have evolved worldwide — and where critical challenges remain.

## Two Centuries of Educational Expansion

In the early 1800s, fewer than 1 in 5 adults worldwide had received any formal education. Education was a luxury reserved for a small elite. Over the past two centuries, this ratio has reversed dramatically. Today, more than 4 in 5 adults (aged 15+) have received some formal primary, secondary, or tertiary education. Literacy rates have followed a similar trajectory: two centuries ago, very few could read and write; now, the vast majority of adults possess basic literacy skills.

## The Learning Crisis: Being in School ≠ Learning

International statistics often track enrollment and attendance as markers of progress. However, being enrolled does not guarantee quality learning. In many lower-income countries, fewer than 20% of children achieve minimum reading proficiency by the end of primary school — meaning they cannot identify key ideas in a text or connect them to their own experiences. The data reveals a stark learning crisis hidden behind enrollment numbers.

## 244 Million Children Still Out of School

Despite enormous progress, approximately 244 million children of official school age were not enrolled in primary or secondary education in 2023. A major driver is secondary-level dropout: many children who complete primary school do not continue. The following table summarizes the scale of the challenge:

| Indicator | Value (2023) |
|---|---|
| Children out of school (all levels) | ~244 million |
| Primary-age children out of school | ~60 million |
| Secondary-age adolescents out of school | ~184 million |

## Learning-Adjusted Years of Schooling: A World Divided

Researchers combine the quantity and quality of education into a single metric called "learning-adjusted years of schooling." The disparities are enormous:

| Country Group | Learning-Adjusted Years of Schooling (2020) |
|---|---|
| Poorest countries (parts of Sub-Saharan Africa) | < 3 years |
| South Asia & Sub-Saharan Africa average | < 7 years |
| High-income countries | 10+ years |

Children in the world's poorest nations receive less than a third of the quality schooling available to their peers in wealthy countries. Most of the world's children live in South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa, where the average remains below 7 years.

## Closing the Gender Gap

Historically, boys were far more likely to attend school than girls. Today, the global gender gap in enrollment has largely closed across primary and secondary education. At the tertiary level, young women are now more likely to be enrolled than young men.

| Education Level | Gender Gap Status (2023) |
|---|---|
| Primary | Nearly closed globally |
| Secondary | Nearly closed globally |
| Tertiary | Women now exceed men in enrollment |

However, significant exceptions persist. In countries like Afghanistan, girls remain far less likely to attend school at any level.

## Key Takeaway

The world has achieved remarkable progress — but the job is far from done. Hundreds of millions of children are either out of school or learning very little while in it. Closing the gap between enrollment and actual learning, and between rich and poor nations, is one of the most pressing challenges of our time.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate A1 portrait poster: The State of Global Education."""

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import math

# A1 portrait at 150 DPI (good balance of quality and speed)
DPI = 150
W = int(23.39 * DPI)  # 3509
H = int(33.11 * DPI)  # 4967

# Colors
BG = (30, 34, 54)          # deep navy
BG_CARD = (40, 46, 72)     # slightly lighter card bg
AMBER = (255, 179, 71)     # warm amber accent
CORAL = (255, 107, 107)    # coral for crisis/urgency
WHITE = (255, 255, 255)
LIGHT = (200, 210, 230)    # light text
GREEN = (100, 200, 140)    # progress/positive
MUTED = (140, 150, 175)    # muted text
DIVIDER = (60, 68, 100)

# Fonts
def font(size, bold=False):
    if bold:
        try:
            return ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/opentype/inter/Inter-Bold.otf", size)
        except:
            return ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/lato/Lato-Bold.ttf", size)
    try:
        return ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/opentype/inter/Inter-Regular.otf", size)
    except:
        return ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/lato/Lato-Regular.ttf", size)

def font_medium(size):
    try:
        return ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/opentype/inter/Inter-Medium.otf", size)
    except:
        return ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/lato/Lato-Medium.ttf", size)

def font_light(size):
    try:
        return ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/opentype/inter/Inter-Light.otf", size)
    except:
        return ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/lato/Lato-Light.ttf", size)

img = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), BG)
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

MARGIN = 180
content_w = W - 2 * MARGIN
y = 120

# === HEADER ===
# Thin top accent line
draw.rectangle([0, 0, W, 8], fill=AMBER)

# Title
title_font = font(105, bold=True)
subtitle_font = font_light(46)

title = "The State of Global Education"
draw.text((MARGIN, y), title, fill=WHITE, font=title_font)
y += 130
subtitle = "Progress, Gaps, and Inequality"
draw.text((MARGIN, y), subtitle, fill=AMBER, font=font_medium(60))
y += 90

# One-liner
desc = "A comparative look at how far the world has come in expanding education\naccess — and the critical gaps that remain in quality, attendance, and equity."
draw.text((MARGIN, y), desc, fill=LIGHT, font=font_light(36))
y += 110

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, W - MARGIN, y + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y += 50

# === SECTION 1: Historical Progress ===
def draw_section_header(y, title_text, color=AMBER):
    draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 6, y + 50], fill=color)
    draw.text((MARGIN + 24, y + 2), title_text, fill=WHITE, font=font(52, bold=True))
    return y + 75

y = draw_section_header(y, "Two Centuries of Educational Expansion")

# Big "then vs now" comparison
box_w = (content_w - 80) // 2
box_h = 340

# 1800 box
x1 = MARGIN
draw.rounded_rectangle([x1, y, x1 + box_w, y + box_h], radius=20, fill=BG_CARD)
draw.text((x1 + 40, y + 30), "1800", fill=MUTED, font=font_medium(38))
draw.text((x1 + 40, y + 80), "< 1 in 5", fill=CORAL, font=font(90, bold=True))
draw.text((x1 + 40, y + 190), "adults had received\nany formal education", fill=LIGHT, font=font_light(36))

# Today box
x2 = MARGIN + box_w + 80
draw.rounded_rectangle([x2, y, x2 + box_w, y + box_h], radius=20, fill=BG_CARD)
draw.text((x2 + 40, y + 30), "TODAY", fill=MUTED, font=font_medium(38))
draw.text((x2 + 40, y + 80), "> 4 in 5", fill=GREEN, font=font(90, bold=True))
draw.text((x2 + 40, y + 190), "adults have received\nsome formal education", fill=LIGHT, font=font_light(36))

# Arrow between boxes
arrow_x = MARGIN + box_w + 10
arrow_y = y + box_h // 2
for i in range(5):
    draw.polygon([
        (arrow_x + 15, arrow_y - 18 + i),
        (arrow_x + 50, arrow_y + i),
        (arrow_x + 15, arrow_y + 18 + i)
    ], fill=AMBER)

y += box_h + 30

# Progress bar visualization
draw.text((MARGIN, y), "Education access over two centuries:", fill=MUTED, font=font_medium(30))
y += 45
bar_h = 40
# 1800 bar ~20%
draw.rounded_rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + content_w, y + bar_h], radius=10, fill=BG_CARD)
bar_1800 = int(content_w * 0.18)
draw.rounded_rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + bar_1800, y + bar_h], radius=10, fill=(180, 90, 90))
draw.text((MARGIN + bar_1800 + 15, y + 5), "~18% (1800)", fill=MUTED, font=font(26))
y += bar_h + 12
# Today bar ~86%
draw.rounded_rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + content_w, y + bar_h], radius=10, fill=BG_CARD)
bar_today = int(content_w * 0.86)
draw.rounded_rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + bar_today, y + bar_h], radius=10, fill=GREEN)
draw.text((MARGIN + bar_today + 15, y + 5), "~86% (today)", fill=MUTED, font=font(26))
y += bar_h + 60

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, W - MARGIN, y + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y += 50

# === SECTION 2: 244 MILLION — THE DOMINANT STAT ===
y = draw_section_header(y, "Children Still Out of School", CORAL)

# Giant number — visually dominant
big_num_font = font(200, bold=True)
draw.text((MARGIN, y - 10), "244", fill=CORAL, font=big_num_font)
# "million" next to it
draw.text((MARGIN + 620, y + 60), "million", fill=CORAL, font=font(100, bold=True))
draw.text((MARGIN + 620, y + 170), "children not in school (2023)", fill=LIGHT, font=font_medium(40))
y += 260

# Breakdown boxes
breakdown_w = (content_w - 60) // 2
bh = 160

# Primary
draw.rounded_rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + breakdown_w, y + bh], radius=16, fill=BG_CARD)
draw.text((MARGIN + 30, y + 20), "PRIMARY AGE", fill=MUTED, font=font_medium(28))
draw.text((MARGIN + 30, y + 60), "~60M", fill=AMBER, font=font(70, bold=True))

# Secondary
x2 = MARGIN + breakdown_w + 60
draw.rounded_rectangle([x2, y, x2 + breakdown_w, y + bh], radius=16, fill=BG_CARD)
draw.text((x2 + 30, y + 20), "SECONDARY AGE", fill=MUTED, font=font_medium(28))
draw.text((x2 + 30, y + 60), "~184M", fill=AMBER, font=font(70, bold=True))

y += bh + 20
draw.text((MARGIN, y), "Secondary-level dropout is the major driver — many children who complete primary school do not continue.",
          fill=MUTED, font=font_light(30))
y += 60

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, W - MARGIN, y + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y += 50

# === SECTION 3: Learning Crisis ===
y = draw_section_header(y, "The Learning Crisis: Enrollment ≠ Learning")

# Icon array: 20 squares, <20% highlighted
draw.text((MARGIN, y), "In low-income countries, children achieving minimum reading proficiency:", fill=LIGHT, font=font_light(32))
y += 55

icon_size = 52
icon_gap = 14
icons_per_row = 20
for i in range(20):
    ix = MARGIN + i * (icon_size + icon_gap)
    color = CORAL if i < 4 else BG_CARD  # <20% = 4 out of 20
    draw.rounded_rectangle([ix, y, ix + icon_size, y + icon_size], radius=8, fill=color)
    # Person icon simplified as a circle + rectangle
    cx = ix + icon_size // 2
    draw.ellipse([cx - 8, y + 8, cx + 8, y + 24], fill=WHITE if i < 4 else MUTED)
    draw.rounded_rectangle([cx - 11, y + 26, cx + 11, y + 46], radius=4, fill=WHITE if i < 4 else MUTED)

y += icon_size + 20
draw.text((MARGIN, y), "< 20%", fill=CORAL, font=font(50, bold=True))
draw.text((MARGIN + 180, y + 10), "of children reach minimum reading proficiency by end of primary school",
          fill=LIGHT, font=font_light(32))
y += 80

# Divider
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, W - MARGIN, y + 2], fill=DIVIDER)
y += 50

# === SECTION 4: Quality Inequality — Side by Side ===
y = draw_section_header(y, "Learning-Adjusted Years of Schooling: A World Divided")

# Bold bar comparison
bar_label_font = font_medium(34)
bar_val_font = font(70, bold=True)

entries = [
    ("Poorest countries", 2.8, 10, CORAL, "< 3 years"),
    ("South Asia & Sub-Saharan Africa", 6.5, 10, AMBER, "< 7 years"),
    ("High-income countries", 10.5, 10.5, GREEN, "10+ years"),
]

bar_max_w = content_w - 400
for label, val, max_val, color, text in entries:
    draw.text((MARGIN, y + 5), label, fill=LIGHT, font=bar_label_font)
    y += 48
    bw = int((val / 12) * bar_max_w)
    draw.rounded_rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + bar_max_w, y + 56], radius=12, fill=BG_CARD)
    draw.rounded_rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + bw, y + 56], radius=12, fill=color)
    draw.text((MARGIN + bw + 20, y + 2), text, fill=color, font=font(42, bold=True))
    y += 78

y += 10
# Callout box
callout_h = 110
draw.rounded_rectangle([MARGIN, y, W - MARGIN, y + callout_h], radius=16, fill=(60, 30, 30))
draw.rectangle([MARGIN, y, MARGIN + 8, y + callout_h], fill=CORAL)
draw.text((MARGIN + 30, y + 18), "Children in the poorest nations receive less than a third", fill=WHITE, font=font_medium(36))
draw.text((MARGIN + 30, y + 62), "of the quality schooling available in wealthy countries.", fill=LIGHT, font=font_light(36))
